topic: How to stay productive at work (the switching tax) - Activate

slides.headline:
You're not
*unfocused*.
Your workday
is just
switching tasks
all day.

In real offices,
a new task
starts every
**3 minutes**.
slides.subtitle: work fragments faster than any to-do list

note: Mark et al., 2005, 'No Task Left Behind?'

slides.headline:
Every switch
leaves a
residue. Half
your mind
**stays behind**.
slides.subtitle: your next work task pays the tax before it starts

note: Leroy, 2009, Org. Behav. Human Decision Processes

slides.headline:
It can take
**23 minutes**
to refocus
after one
interruption.
slides.subtitle: the average pause before work focus fully returns

note: Gloria Mark, UC Irvine, research on interrupted work

slides.headline:
Never switch
work tasks
empty-handed:
jot the
**next step**.
slides.subtitle: tested on real work tasks - planning restored focus

note: Leroy, 2009, Org. Behav. Human Decision Processes

slides.headline:
Productivity
at work isn't
doing more
all day.
It's
**finishing**.
slides.subtitle: save this - and pick tomorrow's one real finish
